key_insight: 4D particle tracking revealed that mixing in a baffled stirred tank is strongly anisotropic and organized into five coherent fluid compartments that hinder exchange.
engineering_relevance: These transport barriers help explain nonuniform substrate distribution and can guide reactor design and operating conditions for better mixing in chemical and biochemical processes.
method: Tracked up to 40,000 tracer particles in a 3 L stirred tank with two Rushton turbines and three baffles.
Computed Lagrangian velocities, accelerations, and spatial dispersion from time-resolved 4D trajectories.
Applied network-based analysis to identify coherent compartments and weak inter-compartment exchange.
evidence_signal: The study uses full-volume, time-resolved experimental particle trajectories and reports freely available data for direct reference and reuse.
watch_item: The results come from a specific laboratory-scale reactor geometry, so compartment patterns may not transfer directly to other impeller or baffle configurations.
paper_title: Can we live Danckwerts' dream? Mixing Analysis in a Baffled Stirred Tank Reactor Based on 4D-Particle Tracking Experiments
